name: Sky Tonight
shortDescription: The real night sky over your place, tonight, on your phone or your screen.
description: A planetarium page for your town: every star to magnitude 6 in its true color and brightness, the constellations drawn as glowing lines, the planets, and the Moon in its real phase, over a horizon with the compass points. It opens on tonight's sky, then turns time forward and back so the stars wheel and leave trails. Drag to look around, scroll or pinch to zoom, slide the time ribbon through the night, and tap a star for its name, distance, and constellation. On a phone, hold it up and the sky follows. The Tonight card lists sunset, full dark, the Moon's phase and rise or set, and the planets that are up. Pick deep night, red light for the telescope, or a paper star chart. Everything is computed on the page from the star catalog and the clock; nothing is sent anywhere.
setup: Your agent asks, in one message, where you are (a town or coordinates), whether you want constellation lines and names on, and which look you like: deep night, red light to keep your eyes adapted to the dark, or a paper star chart. It works out the time zone from your place. No keys or accounts are needed, and the page calls no service: the star catalog, the Milky Way, and the Moon map ship with it.
